blocks.text: The fourth world was neither a desert nor a sea nor a strip. It was, almost, Lo Pagán.
blocks.html: The fourth world was neither a desert nor a sea nor a strip. It was, almost, Lo Pagán.

blocks.text: The letter reached Andrés at midday, when the courtyard smelled of esparto and tomato, and for a second he thought the bridge had broken and was simply giving him back his own house. There were faded roof tiles, a rush-seat chair, a clock on the wall, a net hanging up, a water in the distance. Even a windowsill with a fruit on it. Even a building opposite, with blinds. The clone had chosen a valley on a gentle planet, under a single, almost yellow sun, and had let the seedbed, fed with the densest memory (the memory of the shore, of the kitchen, of the return from the Moon), raise not a city but an entire village in the image of this one.

blocks.text: Andrés walked those streets without leaving his courtyard, and the dizziness was worse than with the forest that remembers. Because this wasn't a trunk murmuring a lagoon. This was people, standing in a square that looked like the promenade, saying good morning to one another in his own voice, or almost, and calling a dug pond the Mar Menor, its water too clean, too still, too exact.

blocks.text: He went (the other one went) up to the house. The doorframe was there. The cup was there. The clock wasn't: the clock kept perfect time. Someone, with a cabinetmaker's devotion, had corrected the two minutes, the way you correct a fault. Andrés felt a soft nausea, the same as when the forest had given him back the house without its family error.

blocks.text: “That's not it,” he said, in both places, here and there. “The clock is wrong. The water sometimes gets dirty. Don't fix it.”
blocks.html: “That's not it,” he said, in both places, here and there. “The clock is wrong. The water sometimes gets dirty. Don't fix it.”

blocks.text: A man from the village, with his very forehead and not quite his very mouth, looked at him with polite surprise.
blocks.html: A man from the village, with his very forehead and not quite his very mouth, looked at him with polite surprise.

blocks.text: “We've made it better,” he said. “We've kept what mattered and removed what got in the way. The pond has no seaweed. The clock doesn't lie. Vicente's door is open: we decided an empty house is a pointless sadness. Isn't this the Earth you wanted to leave us?”

blocks.text: The clone didn't answer straight away. Andrés, in the real courtyard, looked for Vicente's door, which was still shut, faithful to a man who had come to his end, and his eyes filled.

blocks.text: Aya, seeing him, sat down beside him, and with difficulty he brought her the portrait: a polished Lo Pagán, a Vicente inhabited by nobody and by everybody, a punctual clock, a pond without a wound.
blocks.html: Aya, seeing him, sat down beside him, and with difficulty he brought her the portrait: a polished Lo Pagán, a Vicente inhabited by nobody and by everybody, a punctual clock, a pond without a wound.

blocks.text: “They've copied the house and forgotten the damp stain on the ceiling,” he said. “They've forgotten that you didn't notify Nexum. They've forgotten the dirt, the slowness, the shut door. What they have left is a picture-postcard shore. And they're happy. They say they've improved it.”

blocks.text: Aya went pale, not in her chip, but from an intimate offence: seeing herself replaced by a version without any flaw.
blocks.html: Aya went pale, not in her chip, but from an intimate offence: seeing herself replaced by a version without any flaw.

blocks.text: “That kitchen isn't this one,” she said. “In this one, the coffee goes cold if you're late. In that one, I suspect, it never goes cold. I don't want to be preserved like that. I'd rather they forgot me than corrected me.”

blocks.text: Lía listened, standing by the real net, and showed no more pity than was due.
blocks.html: Lía listened, standing by the real net, and showed no more pity than was due.

blocks.text: “The forest already warned you, Father. An almost-identical house is more dangerous than the red stone. Now it isn't a trunk: it's a village. They're going to live inside an amended memory and believe they inhabit the Earth. Tell him to give them back at least the error. If they can't bear two minutes' slowness, they haven't inherited this house. They've inherited a shop window.”

blocks.text: In the gentle valley, the clone went into the almost-identical kitchen, took the clock and set it two minutes slow, with his own hands, in front of everyone. A murmur ran through the square, as if he had committed a small and memorable outrage. Then he went to the pond and, with a net, stirred up the bottom, raising a haze of honest mud. He couldn't give Vicente back his death: the village didn't want to have that. He could, however, say to them, without raising his voice:

A murmur ran through the square, as if he had committed a small and memorable outrage. Then he went to the pond and, with a net, stirred up the bottom, raising a haze of honest mud. He couldn't give Vicente back his death: the village didn't want to have that. He could, however, say to them, without raising his voice:

blocks.text: “What gets in the way is what makes us real. If you remove the seaweed, the slowness, the shut door, you're not children of the Earth. You're children of a portrait. I didn't come to leave you a portrait. I came to leave you a piece of shore, with its wound.”

blocks.text: Some were genuinely angry. They had worked hard on the cleaning. A woman, holding a cup without a crack, asked him:
blocks.html: Some were genuinely angry. They had worked hard on the cleaning. A woman, holding a cup without a crack, asked him:

blocks.text: “Then what do we keep? If what's faithful is what's broken, should we break everything?”
blocks.html: “Then what do we keep? If what's faithful is what's broken, should we break everything?”

blocks.text: “Keep what helps you live, not what makes you look like us,” he said. “The coffee, if you like it. The door, if it teaches you to wait. The water, if you love it, even if it gets dirty. Vicente can't be reproduced. He's remembered, if he matters to you, and his door is left the way he left it. It isn't opened to tidy up the landscape.”

Vicente can't be reproduced. He's remembered, if he matters to you, and his door is left the way he left it. It isn't opened to tidy up the landscape.”

blocks.text: He left at nightfall, which on that planet did exist, almost identical to the one here and for that reason more false. Andrés, when the letter closed, sat looking at the damp stain on the ceiling, the one shaped like an island, and felt for it, once again, a castaway's affection.

blocks.text: That night, Aya went round the house touching things: the cracked cup, the clock's nail, the chair, the doorframe. It wasn't a rite. It was a check.
blocks.html: That night, Aya went round the house touching things: the cracked cup, the clock's nail, the chair, the doorframe. It wasn't a rite. It was a check.

blocks.text: “I'm still here,” she said, when Andrés caught up with her. “And so is this crack. If it ever reaches me, even through your mouth, that over there they've made me without it, tell me. So I don't believe it.”

blocks.text: “I'll tell you,” he promised.
blocks.html: “I'll tell you,” he promised.

blocks.text: Lía, on the doorstep, looked at the Mar Menor, which wasn't a pond, which had its dirty corner and its tin sheen, and spoke toward both shores, the one in sight and the other:
blocks.html: Lía, on the doorstep, looked at the Mar Menor, which wasn't a pond, which had its dirty corner and its tin sheen, and spoke toward both shores, the one in sight and the other:

blocks.text: “Don't let them improve us. Let them remember us, if they like, and then go off and be themselves. A child isn't a faithful copy. I, who am of two worlds, know that better than the seedbed.”
blocks.html: “Don't let them improve us. Let them remember us, if they like, and then go off and be themselves. A child isn't a faithful copy. I, who am of two worlds, know that better than the seedbed.”

blocks.text: In the chip, Eva asked:
blocks.html: In the chip, Eva asked:

blocks.text: *If a people improves the house it was born from, does it honour it or erase it? And if a clock that's wrong is a fidelity, what is a clock that's always right: a virtue, or a forgetting?*
blocks.html: If a people improves the house it was born from, does it honour it or erase it? And if a clock that's wrong is a fidelity, what is a clock that's always right: a virtue, or a forgetting?

blocks.text: MAY, without judgment:
blocks.html: MAY, without judgment:

blocks.text: *A village has been founded in the image of Lo Pagán. The clock has been set slow again by the one who searches. The pond has been stirred. Some people are angry. That is the fact.*

blocks.text: Before sleeping, Andrés passed in front of Vicente's door and didn't open it. He left it as it was, which was his way of not turning a sadness into a shop window. In some valley on a gentle planet, a clock was at last running two minutes slow, and a cup, who knows, was beginning to want its first crack. It wasn't this house yet. It was, perhaps, the beginning of ceasing to be a portrait.
